title: The Cedar Bench
subtitle: Seven boards, four lengths, one stacked bench

chapters.title: Seven Boards, Four Lengths
chapters.blurb: The cutting schedule as a machine: seven eight-foot cedar boards consumed into six 48s, five 18s, twelve 14-and-a-halfs and five little blocks, with almost nothing left over.

chapters.title: Clamp It Before You Glue It
chapters.blurb: The dry run that costs ten minutes and saves a board: clamps before glue, a level that keeps coming back, and sanding the faces you will never reach again.

chapters.title: The Stack Is the Joint
chapters.blurb: Eight glued courses with no mortise and no tenon — and the geometry that explains why the two-inch screws get retired partway up the stack.

chapters.title: Dowels, Not Screw Heads
chapters.blurb: A countersink half an inch deep, a glued dowel, a pull-saw cut flush, and the moment the screw holes turn into the pattern that defines the bench.
